# Results — Study 629 (Congress Trading)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test
(Ziobrowski et al. 2004) — **US senators' stock purchases beat the market** — retested on the
modern disclosed tape: every stock purchase in the **Senate Stock Watcher** PTR archive, entered
at the first close **after the public disclosure** (the only trade a member of the public can
replicate). Abnormal returns vs **SPY** (both total-return); the verdict statistic is a
**calendar-time portfolio Newey-West t** (the standard fix for overlapping event windows).
Offline & deterministic once cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.
As-of **2026-07-03** (the tape itself ends 2022-12-30 — see coverage). Fingerprint
`884027dc84c9`.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Events | **2,776** disclosed stock purchases, disclosures **2015-01-05 → 2021-03-09**, **26 senators** (Senate Stock Watcher per-day PTR reports; the scraper stopped updating in March 2021) |
| Party mix | R **1,990** / D **786** (Angus King, I, grouped with the D caucus) |
| Concentration | **David Perdue alone = 39.3%** of all events; famous subset (Perdue, Loeffler, Inhofe — the 2020 DOJ-probe names on this tape) = **1,212** events (43.7%) |
| Reporting lag | median **19 days**, mean **26.3 days** from trade to public disclosure — by the time you can copy it, the trade is ~3 weeks old |
| Prices | yfinance daily **auto-adjusted (total-return)** closes, 2013-06-03 → 2022-12-30 (2,414 days); **438** tickers resolved on Yahoo, **1** dropped by the recycled-ticker integrity guard (ITC), **437** used + SPY |
| Event coverage | **2,221 of 2,776 (80.0%)** events have a resolvable ticker + a full 12-month forward window |
| Execution / costs | exactly **one execution lag**: buy at the first close **strictly after** the disclosure date; long-only (no borrow); **0 / 5 / 10 bps** one-way × 2 legs spread over the hold |

> **Survivorship (named on the Signal axis).** ~20% of disclosed purchases drop out because the
> ticker no longer resolves on Yahoo (delisted, acquired, renamed — CELG, TWTR, FEYE, DISCA…).
> Senators' picks that later *died* are under-represented, which biases the measured buy-alpha
> **up** — and the verdict below is a *no* even with that tailwind. **Coverage caveats:** the
> window is 2015–2021 (post-STOCK-Act, the scraper stopped in March 2021), so this tape cannot
> speak to Ziobrowski's 1993–1998 sample — only to the modern disclosed record; and one senator
> (Perdue) is 39% of the sample, so a Perdue-excluded aggregate is reported.

## Event study — the pooled per-event view (color only)

Per-event buy-and-hold abnormal return vs SPY from the post-disclosure entry close. Event
windows **overlap and cluster** by senator and by day, so the naive t **overstates** — quoted
as color, never as the verdict.

| horizon | mean abnormal vs SPY | naive t | n |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 63 td (~3 mo) | **−0.14%** | −0.46 | 2,221 |
| 126 td (~6 mo) | **+1.07%** | +2.33 | 2,221 |
| 252 td (~12 mo) | **+4.87%** | +6.35 | 2,221 |

The 12-month pooled number *looks* Ziobrowski-sized — that is exactly the illusion the
calendar-time engine below exists to puncture: thousands of overlapping windows re-count the
same few market episodes (above all the 2020–21 rebound under Perdue's clustered 2019–20 buys).

## Calendar-time portfolio — the verdict statistic (PRIMARY)

Each day, hold every stock disclosed-bought in the past `hold` trading days, equal-weighted;
the daily excess return vs SPY is a single non-overlapping series tested with a **Newey-West
t (10 lags)**. Gross, long-only.

| hold | alpha (ann.) | **NW t** | days | avg names held |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 63 td | −0.01%/yr | **−0.00** | 1,617 | 48 |
| 126 td | +3.72%/yr | **+1.11** | 1,680 | 80 |
| 252 td | +2.50%/yr | **+0.89** | 1,806 | 123 |

No horizon comes near the desk's **t ≥ 2** bar. The pooled +4.87%/12-mo collapses to a
**t = 0.89** once overlap is handled honestly.

## Random-dates placebo — is it the timing, or just their stock list?

Re-run the calendar-time engine with the **same tickers** but **random disclosure dates**
(uniform on the tape), averaged over **20 seeds** (hold = 126):

| quantity | value |
|---|--:|
| placebo alpha (same stocks, random timing) | **+3.31%/yr** (sd 0.84) |
| placebo NW t | mean +1.79 (sd 0.43) |
| real alpha − placebo alpha | **+0.41%/yr = +0.49 placebo-sd** |

The senators' thin positive drift is **fully explained by the stocks they happen to hold**
(an equal-weight basket of their names beat cap-weighted SPY over 2015–2022 regardless of
timing). The **disclosure date itself adds +0.4%/yr — statistical zero**. There is no timing
information in the disclosed tape.

## Costs — what a copy-trader nets

One-way costs × 2 legs spread over the 126-td hold (turnover is low; costs are not the
problem — the absence of signal is):

| one-way cost | net alpha (ann.) | NW t |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps | +3.72%/yr | +1.11 |
| 5 bps | +3.52%/yr | +1.05 |
| 10 bps | +3.32%/yr | +0.99 |

## Splits — party, size (Welch t on per-event abnormal returns; color)

| split (h = 126 td) | group | rest | diff | Welch t |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| R vs D | +1.12% (n=1,553) | +0.95% (n=668) | +0.17 pp | **+0.18** |
| big (≥$15k) vs small | +1.52% (n=585) | +0.91% (n=1,636) | +0.60 pp | **+0.56** |
| famous vs rest | +0.59% (n=840) | +1.36% (n=1,381) | −0.77 pp | **−0.79** |

At h = 252: R−D +0.43 pp (t = +0.26); big−small −1.79 pp (t = −1.10); famous−rest **+7.61 pp
(t = +4.57)** — see the third axis for why that last number is an artifact.

## Third axis — do the famous names (the meme) beat the boring aggregate?

The meme says the scandal names are the alpha. The pooled 12-month view even agrees:
famous **+9.61%** vs boring **+1.99%**, Welch **t = +4.57**. But per-event Welch assumes
independent events, and the famous subset is **840 massively overlapping windows** —
mostly Perdue's clustered 2019–20 buys re-counting the *single* 2020–21 rebound (the same
split flips **negative**, −0.77 pp, at 6 months). The calendar-time engine, which exists to
fix exactly this, says:

| aggregate (hold = 126) | alpha (ann.) | NW t |
|---|--:|--:|
| **FAMOUS** (Perdue, Loeffler, Inhofe) | **+0.09%/yr** | **+0.02** |
| **BORING** (the other 23 senators) | +4.66%/yr | +1.85 |
| ex-Perdue aggregate | +4.75%/yr | +1.87 |

The famous names' calendar-time alpha is **exactly zero**. What weak, sub-significant drift
exists on this tape lives in the *boring* rest — the meme is **BUSTED**.

## Synthetic control — the machinery is faithful

Deterministic market + stocks + events world; the planted knob is a post-disclosure drift on
the bought name. *(Machinery proof only — never cited as market evidence.)*

| world | calendar-time result |
|---|---|
| null (edge = 0), **20 seeds** | mean NW t = **+0.03**, sd 0.97, max \|t\| = 2.10 — no manufactured significance |
| planted +6 bps/day drift (1 seed shown) | alpha **+27.37%/yr**, NW t = **+12.25** — lights up |

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The replicable trade (buy at the post-disclosure close) earns a
  calendar-time alpha of **−0.0 to +3.7%/yr** with **NW t ≤ 1.11** at every horizon — nowhere
  near t ≥ 2 — and the random-dates placebo shows even that thin drift is the **stock list, not
  the timing** (real − placebo = +0.4%/yr, +0.49 sd). The Ziobrowski-sized pooled 12-mo number
  (+4.87%, naive t 6.35) is an overlap illusion. All this on a **survivor-tilted** panel that
  *helps* the claim. The modern disclosed tape does not agree with Ziobrowski.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is nothing to deploy: the information is a median **19 days
  stale** at disclosure, the alpha is statistically zero and indistinguishable from random
  timing, and costs (small as they are here) only subtract. Copy-trading senators, at least on
  2015–2021 Senate purchase disclosures, buys you an equal-weight stock basket — not an edge.
- **"The famous names are the alpha"? — BUSTED.** Famous-subset calendar-time alpha
  **+0.09%/yr (t = 0.02)** vs boring **+4.66%/yr (t = 1.85)**; the meme's spectacular pooled
  premium (+7.6 pp at 12 mo, Welch t = 4.6) is a clustering artifact of one senator's
  overlapping 2019–20 buys riding one rebound.
